text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they frequently add it to a shared project. This action automatically starts a build, which means the software is compiled and prepared for use. As part of this process, automated tests run to check if the new code works correctly and does not break anything else. CI pipelines help organise these steps, from building to testing. The main benefit is catching issues early, before they become bigger problems. This saves time and makes the software more reliable.
